fields.artDirection: Art direction (fixed; from design/style-guide/README.md and design/art-direction.md). The look is Miniature Lives: a sculpted, rounded, tactile creature with soft materials, directional light, expressive eyes and clear markings, alive and physical even when small; saturated, playful colour with clear highlights, never dull brown or grey. The treatment is the Station's: full resolution, one key light from the top left, soft form shading, painted gradients, three or four principal value masses, restrained highlights, the eyes as flat inks with one catch light, a friendly small face, a fine pixel grain, no dither bands, no flat fills. Art never changes genes: the painter may not add, remove, move, turn or resize a part, change the pose or the proportions, move a pigment out of its slot or change a marking; the painter adds surface, light and life only. The subject stands alone on a flat uniform ground of exactly #f6f3ec: no scene, no ground, no cast shadow, no props, no text, no border, the same size and in the same place as in the form image.
fields.controls: Paint the creature in image 1 exactly as it is drawn: the same silhouette, pose, camera, proportions and framing, every part present, no part added, nothing turned. Image 1 is its form under one light from the top left. Image 2 is the colour key: the same body with every area flat in the exact pigment it must be painted in; paint each area in a ramp of that colour and no other, never moved, never swapped: body → #4d7ed4, second → #fff0b8, eyeRim → #f1eddc, pupil → #273036. Image 3 is the part map: its colours are labels, not paint; each flat colour is one part of the same body (region-0, region-1, neck, head, beak, eye, crown, leg-0, flap, tail); keep every part exactly where it is, at the same size, facing the same way. The creature stands still, seen from the front quarter, its face toward the viewer's left, as in image 1.
fields.description: A juvenile Belatz: 2 body regions (B2), a head, 2 eyes, a 2-leaf crest, 2 legs, 2 flaps, a tail; feathers; upright, neck head. It is the type of its kind, a big bird: wings and a beak; big birds of open sky. Coat: colour cobalt; fluff between; sheen between; feathers between; fur reach body only; second colour butter. Face: head between; beak between; crest between; crown tall; eyes small, close. Shape: waist thick; back line level; hind body between; body egg; build between. Legs & tail: tail curl straight; tail between. Proportions: a large body, the head carried high, small eyes, a tall crest, long legs, broad feet, a thick waist, wide flaps.

The treatment is the Station's: full resolution, one key light from the top left, soft form shading, painted gradients, three or four principal value masses, restrained highlights, the eyes as flat inks with one catch light, a friendly small face, a fine pixel grain, no dither bands, no flat fills. Art never changes genes: the painter may not add, remove, move, turn or resize a part, change the pose or the proportions, move a pigment out of its slot or change a marking; the painter adds surface, light and life only. The subject stands alone on a flat uniform ground of exactly #f6f3ec: no scene, no ground, no cast shadow, no props, no text, no border, the same size and in the same place as in the form image.
fields.controls: Paint the creature in image 1 exactly as it is drawn: the same silhouette, pose, camera, proportions and framing, every part present, no part added, nothing turned. Image 1 is its form under one light from the top left. Image 2 is the colour key: the same body with every area flat in the exact pigment it must be painted in; paint each area in a ramp of that colour and no other, never moved, never swapped: body → #465459, second → #dfd2ae, eyeRim → #f1eddc, pupil → #273036, belly → #dfd2ae. Image 3 is the part map: its colours are labels, not paint; each flat colour is one part of the same body (region-0, head, muzzle, eye, leg-0, leg-1); keep every part exactly where it is, at the same size, facing the same way. The creature stands still, seen in profile from its right side, the head facing right, as in image 1.
fields.description: A juvenile Loika: 1 body region (B1), a head, a snout, 2 eyes, 4 legs; skin; plantigrade, fused head. Coat: markings plain. Face: crown bare head; eye rings between. Proportions: a big head, the head carried high, a short muzzle, a tall crest, short legs, stout legs, broad feet, a stout build.
fields.reference: Image 4 is the accepted painting of Pip, the Loika's type specimen (art/miniature-lives): the finished look to match exactly, its treatment, its materials, its face and how the light falls on it. This creature is one of that kind and differs from it only as the description and the drawings say. Image 5 is this same creature already painted from the front quarter: match its colours, surfaces, markings and face exactly, so the two views are one creature.

The look is Miniature Lives: a sculpted, rounded, tactile creature with soft materials, directional light, expressive eyes and clear markings, alive and physical even when small; saturated, playful colour with clear highlights, never dull brown or grey. The treatment is the Station's: full resolution, one key light from the top left, soft form shading, painted gradients, three or four principal value masses, restrained highlights, the eyes as flat inks with one catch light, a friendly small face, a fine pixel grain, no dither bands, no flat fills. Art never changes genes: the painter may not add, remove, move, turn or resize a part, change the pose or the proportions, move a pigment out of its slot or change a marking; the painter adds surface, light and life only. The subject stands alone on a flat uniform ground of exactly #f6f3ec: no scene, no ground, no cast shadow, no props, no text, no border, the same size and in the same place as in the form image.

Paint the creature in image 1 exactly as it is drawn: the same silhouette, pose, camera, proportions and framing, every part present, no part added, nothing turned. Image 1 is its form under one light from the top left. Image 2 is the colour key: the same body with every area flat in the exact pigment it must be painted in; paint each area in a ramp of that colour and no other, never moved, never swapped: body → #465459, second → #dfd2ae, eyeRim → #f1eddc, pupil → #273036, belly → #dfd2ae. Image 3 is the part map: its colours are labels, not paint; each flat colour is one part of the same body (region-0, head, muzzle, eye, crown, leg-0, leg-1); keep every part exactly where it is, at the same size, facing the same way. The creature stands still, seen in profile from its right side, the head facing right, as in image 1. The drawings show structure and proportion only: where each part is, how big it is and which colour it carries. Their flat facets, hard edges and small eyes are not the look: render the volume, the softness, the face and the finish as image 4 does, over this structure.

The creature: A juvenile Loika: 1 body region (B1), a head, a snout, 2 eyes, a 3-leaf crest, 4 legs; skin; plantigrade, fused head. Coat: markings plain. Face: crown leaf crest; eye rings thin rings. Proportions: a big head, the head carried high, a short muzzle, small eyes, a tall crest, short legs, stout legs, broad feet, a stout build.

Image 4 is the accepted painting of Pip, the Loika's type specimen (art/miniature-lives): the finished look to match exactly, its treatment, its materials, its face and how the light falls on it. This creature is one of that kind and differs from it only as the description and the drawings say. Image 5 is this same creature already painted from the front quarter: match its colours, surfaces, markings and face exactly, so the two views are one creature.

A previous painting of this creature was rejected because paint lies well outside the drawn body (43% of the body beyond a 20 px band): a part was added, moved or re-laid; part of the drawn body is left unpainted (12% of the body inside a 20 px band): a part was dropped or moved; a part is missing or moved from where the part map puts it: muzzle (0.02), crown (0.00), leg-1 (0.39). This time keep the silhouette of image 1 and the parts of image 3 exactly, part for part.

Output one square image.

part of the drawn body is left unpainted (12% of the body inside a 20 px band): a part was dropped or moved
a part is missing or moved from where the part map puts it: muzzle (0.02), crown (0.00), leg-1 (0.39)

reasons: a pigment slot is painted in another slot's colour: the belly slot on the region-0 (painted #606a68, the colour of body)
